rationale:
DECISION: split into 7 children: 5 new leaves and 2 reused accepted declarations.

WHY. The selected theorem bundles four independent analytic obligations:
- Hausdorff-measure domination on the graph piece (supplied steps 2-4);
- the area comparison and null-set transfer along the graph map (steps 1, 5);
- tangent-plane identification (step 6);
- quadratic Lebesgue points (step 7).
A leaf must be one appended theorem with no helper declarations and no new imports (leaf_verification.check_source_delta), so a monolithic proof is unsafe. Each child below is a reusable statement of leaf size; all 5 new children have already been proved sorry-free in a scratch project.

CHILDREN AND THE SUPPLIED STEPS THEY DISCHARGE
- upper_density = accepted Submission.aetp_upper_density_zero_ae (identical frozen type). This is the Upper Density Theorem of step 3.
- tangent_facts = accepted Submission.ted_tangent_plane_facts (identical frozen type).
  - Conjunct (4) is the locality of approximate tangent planes along Lipschitz graphs (Simon Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(1)), proved by the blow-up argument of step 6.
  - Conjunct (2) is the mu-a.e. strong measurability of p used in step 7 (the same fact as tangent_ae (b)).
- graph_volume: L^n(A) <= H^n(q(graph u over A)), via the 1-Lipschitz left inverse pi o q^-1 (steps 1, 5).
- hausdorff_le_weight (uses upper_density): positive lower density and theta >= 1 give H^n restricted to Gamma <= mu (steps 3-4).
- graph_transfer (uses graph_volume): Lusin–Souslin, (E1) for every nu >= H^n restricted to Gamma, and transfer of nu-null sets to L^n-null parameter sets (steps 1, 5).
- graph_tangent (uses tangent_facts): (E2). It applies tangent_facts (4) to Lipschitz extensions of u on countably many balls in Omega, plus the step-5 transfer (step 6).
- lebesgue_points: Besicovitch differentiation for mu restricted to O, for a bounded operator field, in the hsNormSq form (step 7).

ASSEMBLY OF THE SELECTED THEOREM (checked in Lean, sorry-free)
0. Constants. kappa := (p-n)/(4p), omega := unitBallVolume n > 0, delta_E := min(kappa, kappa omega/2) > 0. For delta <= delta_E: delta <= kappa, and Lambda := 4p delta/(p-n) = delta/kappa <= omega/2. Hence c := e^(-Lambda) (omega - Lambda) > 0.
1. AllardHypotheses gives theta >= 1 mu-a.e. and mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1+delta) omega rho^n < infinity.
2. Lower density. Use (M2) of the parent dependency any_radius_monotonicity_bounds. Let y be in Gamma := q(graph u over Omega), which is contained in spt V cap B°_rho(0), and R := rho - |y|. Then B_R(y) is contained in B_rho(0), so ofReal(c s^n) <= mu(B_s(y)) for 0 < s < R.
3. hausdorff_le_weight with O := B°_rho(0) gives H^n restricted to Gamma <= mu.
4. graph_transfer with nu := mu (Omega is open; u is continuous on Omega). Its part (b) is literally (E1), and its part (c) is the transfer.
5. (E2) is graph_tangent applied with that transfer.
6. (E3) is lebesgue_points with O := B°_rho(0), g := V.tangentProj, C := 1.
   - Measurability comes from tangent_facts (2).
   - ||V.tangentProj w|| <= 1 because V.tangentProj w is a starProjection (Submodule.starProjection_norm_le) or 0.
   - Transfer by (c), using F(x) in Gamma, which is contained in B°_rho(0).
The declared dependency tangent_ae is no longer needed; monotonicity_bounds still is.

DEVIATION FROM THE SUPPLIED TEXT (same conclusions)
- Step 6 is not re-proved with a new blow-up. Instead, the accepted locality theorem, whose proof is that blow-up argument for Lipschitz graphs, is applied to local Lipschitz extensions. Its exceptional set is mu-null rather than H^n-null, and the step-5 transfer covers mu-null sets.
- Step 7 uses the bound ||p_y||_op <= 1, which holds everywhere, instead of |p_y|_HS <= sqrt n mu-a.e.

subproblems.title: Upper density theorem: zero density of a finite measure off a Borel set (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, nu a measure on (the Borel sigma-algebra of) R^(n+l) = Amb n l and A a Borel subset of R^(n+l) with nu(A) < infinity. Then for H^n-almost every x (H^n = muHE[n]) with x not in A, nu(A cap B_r(x)) / r^n tends to 0 in [0, infinity] as r -> 0+ (B_r(x) the closed ball, r^n read as ENNReal.ofReal (r^n)).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration. This child is the already accepted declaration Submission.aetp_upper_density_zero_ae (DAG node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.ae_tangent_planes-a1.upper_density_zero-a1; comparator passed; candidate commit 066406829f5683c27ac3a01e8406376a154ff75a), reused with its identical frozen type, so no new formalization is requested and this proof is informational (the controller keeps the reviewed proof and the Lean proof of the accepted node). It is Simon Ch. 1, Upper Density Theorem 3.6, in Mathlib's normalisation of H^n. A complete self-contained proof follows.

Notation. E := R^(n+l) = Amb n l, a separable metric space with its Borel sigma-algebra; B_r(x) is the closed ball and B°_r(x) the open ball. H^n := muHE[n] = c_n muH[n] with c_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume, muH[n]) in (0, infinity) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def; Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero), so H^n and muH[n] have the same null sets. lambda := nu restricted to A. Since A is Borel, lambda(S) = nu(S cap A) for every Borel S, so lambda(B_r(x)) = nu(A cap B_r(x)), and lambda(E) = nu(A) < infinity: lambda is a finite Borel measure.

1. Reduction. Let x not in A be such that nu(A cap B_r(x))/ofReal(r^n) does not tend to 0 as r -> 0+. Since the intervals [0, t), t > 0, form a neighbourhood basis of 0 in [0, infinity], there is t > 0 such that for every e > 0 some r in (0, e) satisfies lambda(B_r(x)) >= t r^n. Choose an integer k >= 1 with 1/k <= t. Hence the exceptional set is contained in the union over k >= 1 of
   Z_k := {x in E \ A : for every e > 0 there is r in (0, e) with lambda(B_r(x)) >= r^n / k}.
   By countable subadditivity it suffices to prove muH[n](Z_k) = 0 for every k.
2. A small open neighbourhood. Fix k, eta > 0 and d > 0. lambda(Z_k) <= lambda(E \ A) = nu((E \ A) cap A) = 0. A finite Borel measure on a metric space is outer regular (Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure), so there is an open G containing Z_k with lambda(G) < eta (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt). For each x in Z_k choose r_x in (0, d/10) with B_{r_x}(x) contained in G and lambda(B_{r_x}(x)) >= r_x^n / k. To do so, take e_x > 0 with B°_{2 e_x}(x) contained in G (G is open), then apply the definition of Z_k with e := min(e_x, d/10).
3. Vitali covering. Apply the Vitali covering lemma for closed balls, with enlargement factor 5 and radii bounded by d/10 (Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall with tau = 5 > 3). It gives J contained in Z_k such that the balls B_{r_x}(x), x in J, are pairwise disjoint, and for every z in Z_k there is x in J with B_{r_z}(z) contained in B_{5 r_x}(x). In particular Z_k is contained in the union of the B_{5 r_x}(x), x in J.
   J is countable. Fix a countable dense D in E. Each nonempty open ball B°_{r_x}(x), x in J, contains a point d_x of D, and disjointness of the balls makes x -> d_x injective.
4. Estimate. Each B_{5 r_x}(x) has diameter at most 10 r_x < d. Using r_x^n <= k lambda(B_{r_x}(x)), disjointness, countable additivity of lambda, and B_{r_x}(x) contained in G:
   sum over x in J of (10 r_x)^n <= 10^n k sum over x in J of lambda(B_{r_x}(x)) = 10^n k lambda(union over x in J of B_{r_x}(x)) <= 10^n k lambda(G) < 10^n k eta.
   So for every d > 0, Z_k has a countable cover by sets of diameter < d with sum of diam^n <= 10^n k eta. By the definition of Hausdorff measure (Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum along d -> 0), muH[n](Z_k) <= 10^n k eta. Since eta > 0 was arbitrary, muH[n](Z_k) = 0. (For n = 0 the same computation holds with (10 r_x)^0 = 1.)
5. Conclusion. muH[n] vanishes on the union of the Z_k, hence so does H^n = c_n muH[n]. That union contains every x not in A at which nu(A cap B_r(x))/ofReal(r^n) fails to tend to 0. Hence for H^n-a.e. x: if x is not in A, then nu(A cap B_r(x))/ofReal(r^n) -> 0 as r -> 0+. QED
proof_key_steps: Reduce to Z_k: points outside A where nu restricted to A gives B_r(x) mass >= r^n/k for arbitrarily small r
Outer regularity of the finite measure nu restricted to A gives an open G containing Z_k of small measure
Vitali 5r-covering by countably many disjoint closed balls inside G
Sum of (10 r)^n <= 10^n k (nu restricted to A)(G), so muH[n](Z_k) = 0 and H^n(Z_k) = 0

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of contract varifolds incl. locality along Lipschitz graphs (reused accepted declaration)

Then (0) for mu-a.e. x there is a subspace P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7); (1) for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace; (2) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (3) for mu-a.e. x, V.HasDensity x (theta x); (4) for every linear isometry q of R^(n+l), every R in R, L >= 0 and every f : R^n -> R^l that is L-Lipschitz on the closed ball B^n_R(0): for mu-a.e. x, whenever x = q(graphPoint(x', f(x'))) with |x'| < R and f is differentiable at x', p_x is the orthogonal projection onto span{q(graphPoint(v, Df(x') v)) : v in R^n}.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration. This child is the already accepted declaration Submission.ted_tangent_plane_facts (DAG node root.tilt_excess_decay-a1.tangent_plane_facts-a1; comparator passed; candidate commit a8902dc6b193b40a3329c4ecc57e245a8e3c2b7c, where its Lean proof is sorry-free). It is reused with its identical frozen type, so no new formalization is requested and this proof is informational (the controller keeps the reviewed proof and the Lean proof of the accepted node). Conclusions (0)-(4) are numbered in the order of the frozen conjunction; the selected node uses (2) (measurability for step 7) and (4) (tangent planes along graphs for step 6). Its proof of (4) (steps 2-3 below) is exactly the blow-up argument of the selected node's step 6, carried out for Lipschitz graphs. The accepted, independently reviewed proof follows verbatim.

Notation. M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult (theta > 0 on M), mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity(ofReal o theta), p_x := V.tangentProj x. eta_{x,r}(y) := r^{-1}(y - x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). HasWeighted(x, P) abbreviates the contract predicate Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P: finrank P = n and lim_{r -> 0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = theta(x) int_P g dH^n for every g in C_c(R^{n+l}). omega_n := unitBallVolume n; B_r(x) closed ball, B°_r(x) open ball; H^n = muHE[n], which equals Lebesgue measure L^n on R^n and on n-planes.

Cited results. [R1] Rademacher (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableAt-type lemmas in Analysis/Calculus/Rademacher.lean): a map Lipschitz on an open set of R^n is differentiable L^n-a.e. there. [R2] Lebesgue differentiation for locally finite Borel measures on Euclidean space (Simon Ch. 1 Sect. 4; Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub): if lambda is locally finite and g in L^1_loc(lambda), then for lambda-a.e. x, lambda(B_r(x))^{-1} int_{B_r(x)} |g - g(x)| dlambda -> 0. [R3] Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2); SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6): if lambda is Borel regular and finite on compact subsets of an open set W and A is a lambda-measurable subset of W, then limsup_{r -> 0+} lambda(A cap B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x in W \ A. [R4] Area formula for injective Lipschitz maps (Simon Ch. 2 Sect. 3; SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon, area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity): if F is injective and Lipschitz on a Borel set Omega in R^n, then for Borel A in Omega and Borel g >= 0, int_{F(A)} g dH^n = int_A g(F(w)) J_F(w) dw, J_F(w) = det(DF(w)^* DF(w))^{1/2} at differentiability points; for an injective linear map the Jacobian is constant. [R5] Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (using the C^1 approximation theorem, Ch. 2, 1.5): a countably n-rectifiable M satisfies M contained in N_0 cup U_{j>=1} N_j with H^n(N_0) = 0 and each N_j an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold. [R6] SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique: if theta(x) != 0, HasWeighted(x, P) and HasWeighted(x, P') then P = P'. [R7] H^n is invariant under isometries, H^n(rA) = r^n H^n(A), H^n(F(A)) <= (Lip F)^n H^n(A) for Lipschitz F.

Proof.
1. Basic facts. (a) mu(A) = 0 whenever H^n(A cap M) = 0, and mu(R^{n+l} \ M) = 0. (b) mu(K) = int_{M cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for compact K contained in U (contract integrableOn_mult). (c) If x in M and HasWeighted(x, P), then the existential in the definition of tangentProj holds, its chosen witness equals P by [R6] (theta(x) > 0), and p_x = P.starProjection. (d) For x, r > 0, any set A and g nonnegative or integrable: int_{eta_{x,r}(A)} g dH^n = r^{-n} int_A g(eta_{x,r}(z)) dH^n(z) [R7].

2. Graph lemma. Fix q, f, R, L as in conclusion (4); assume R > 0 (otherwise (4) is vacuous). Put Omega := B°^n_R(0), F(w) := q(graphPoint(w, f(w))), Gamma := F(Omega), a := pi o q^{-1} with pi(graphPoint(w, y)) := w. For w in Omega at which f is differentiable put P_w := DF(w)(R^n) = span{q(graphPoint(v, Df(w) v)) : v in R^n}; DF(w) v = q(graphPoint(v, Df(w) v)) is injective, so finrank P_w = n.
Claim: there is an H^n-null set Z such that HasWeighted(x, P_{a(x)}) holds for every x in (M cap Gamma) \ Z (in particular f is differentiable at a(x)).
2.1. On the closed ball, |F(w) - F(w')|^2 = |w - w'|^2 + |f(w) - f(w')|^2 <= (1 + L^2)|w - w'|^2, F is injective and a o F = id with a 1-Lipschitz. Hence for A contained in Omega: L^n(A) <= H^n(F(A)) <= (1 + L^2)^{n/2} L^n(A) [R7]; F maps L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets; Gamma is sigma-compact (hence Borel) and H^n(Gamma) < infinity.
2.2. By [R1] f is differentiable at a.e. w in Omega, with ||Df(w)|| <= L there; let J_F(w) := det(I + Df(w)^T Df(w))^{1/2} in [1, (1 + L^2)^{n/2}] at such points and J_F := 1 elsewhere (bounded Borel). By [R2] for L^n, a.e. w in Omega is a Lebesgue point of J_F. Let Z_1 be the L^n-null set of w in Omega where f is not differentiable or which are not Lebesgue points of J_F; H^n(F(Z_1)) = 0 by 2.1. By [R4], int_{F(A)} g dH^n = int_A g(F(w)) J_F(w) dw for Borel A in Omega and Borel g >= 0.
2.3. Tangent plane of Gamma. Let w in Omega \ Z_1, x := F(w), P := P_w, and g in C_c(R^{n+l}) with spt g in B_K(0), |g| <= G. With Phi_r(z) := (F(w + r z) - F(w))/r, by 1(d) and 2.2,
int_{eta_{x,r}(Gamma)} g dH^n = r^{-n} int_Omega g((F(w') - F(w))/r) J_F(w') dw' = int_{(Omega - w)/r} g(Phi_r(z)) J_F(w + r z) dz.
Since |Phi_r(z)| >= |z| the integrand vanishes for |z| > K, and B_K(0) is contained in (Omega - w)/r for small r. Differentiability gives Phi_r(z) -> DF(w) z for every z, so int_{B_K} g(Phi_r(z)) J_F(w) dz -> int_{R^n} g(DF(w) z) J_F(w) dz by dominated convergence, while |int_{B_K} g(Phi_r(z)) (J_F(w + r z) - J_F(w)) dz| <= G r^{-n} int_{B_{rK}(w)} |J_F - J_F(w)| -> 0 (Lebesgue point). By [R4] for the injective linear map DF(w), int_{R^n} g(DF(w) z) J_F(w) dz = int_P g dH^n. Hence lim_{r -> 0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(Gamma)} g dH^n = int_P g dH^n for all g in C_c. Testing with 0 <= g <= 1 equal to 1 on B_1(0) and supported in B_{1+e}(0), resp. equal to 1 on B_{1-e}(0) and supported in B_1(0), and letting e -> 0, also H^n(Gamma cap B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> 1.
2.4. Densities of the complements. (a) [R3] with W := U, lambda := mu (finite on compacts of U by 1(b)), A := M \ Gamma (mu-measurable): for H^n-a.e. x in U \ (M \ Gamma), in particular H^n-a.e. x in M cap Gamma, r^{-n} int_{(M \ Gamma) cap B_r(x)} theta dH^n = r^{-n} mu((M \ Gamma) cap B_r(x)) -> 0. (b) [R3] with W := R^{n+l}, lambda := H^n restricted to Gamma (finite by 2.1), A := Gamma \ M: for H^n-a.e. x in M, r^{-n} H^n((Gamma \ M) cap B_r(x)) -> 0.
2.5. Lebesgue points of theta. lambda_3 := H^n restricted to M cap Gamma is a finite Borel measure. For each compact K contained in U, theta 1_K is lambda_3-integrable, so by [R2] for lambda_3-a.e. x in the interior of K the averages lambda_3(B_r(x))^{-1} int_{B_r(x)} |theta - theta(x)| dlambda_3 tend to 0 (for small r, B_r(x) is contained in K); exhausting U by countably many such K, this holds for lambda_3-a.e. x in U. At points x in M cap Gamma where 2.3 and 2.4(b) also hold, lambda_3(B_r(x)) <= H^n(Gamma cap B_r(x)) <= 2 omega_n r^n for small r, hence r^{-n} int_{M cap Gamma cap B_r(x)} |theta - theta(x)| dH^n -> 0.
2.6. Let Z be the union of F(Z_1) and the H^n-null exceptional sets of 2.4(a), 2.4(b) and 2.5 (H^n-null because lambda_3-null subsets of M cap Gamma are H^n-null). Let x in (M cap Gamma) \ Z, w := a(x) (so x = F(w), w in Omega \ Z_1), P := P_w, g in C_c with spt g in B_K(0) and |g| <= G, and r so small that B_{Kr}(x) is contained in U. By 1(d),
int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_M g(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z)
= theta(x) r^{-n} int_Gamma g(eta_{x,r} z) dH^n - theta(x) r^{-n} int_{Gamma \ M} g(eta_{x,r} z) dH^n + r^{-n} int_{M cap Gamma} g(eta_{x,r} z)(theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n + r^{-n} int_{M \ Gamma} g(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n.
By 2.3 and 1(d) the first term tends to theta(x) int_P g dH^n; the second is at most theta(x) G r^{-n} H^n((Gamma \ M) cap B_{Kr}(x)) -> 0 by 2.4(b); the third is at most G r^{-n} int_{M cap Gamma cap B_{Kr}(x)} |theta - theta(x)| dH^n -> 0 by 2.5; the fourth is at most G r^{-n} int_{(M \ Gamma) cap B_{Kr}(x)} theta dH^n -> 0 by 2.4(a). Thus HasWeighted(x, P_w), proving the claim.

3. Conclusion (4). With Z from step 2, mu(Z) = 0 by 1(a), and mu(Gamma \ M) = 0. Let x be outside Z cup (Gamma \ M) and suppose x = q(graphPoint(x', f(x'))) with x' in B°^n_R(0) and f differentiable at x'. Then x in M cap Gamma \ Z and a(x) = x', so HasWeighted(x, P_{x'}); by 1(c), p_x = P_{x'}.starProjection with P_{x'} = span(range(v |-> q(graphPoint(v, fderiv f x' v)))). Hence (4) holds for mu-a.e. x.

4. Countable C^1-graph cover of M. By [R5], M is contained in N_0 cup U_j N_j. Let y in N_j and choose a linear isometry q_y with q_y(R^n x {0}) = T_y N_j. By the implicit function theorem there are c in R^n, s > 0, a C^1 map g defined on a neighbourhood of the closed ball B^n_s(c), and an open set W_y containing y such that N_j cap W_y = q_y({graphPoint(w, g(w)) : w in B°^n_s(c)}). By second countability countably many W_y cover N_j. g is Lipschitz on the convex compact set B^n_s(c); extend it componentwise (McShane; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) to a Lipschitz map f : R^n -> R^l and choose R > |c| + s. We obtain countably many (q_k, f_k, R_k) and open balls B_k := B°^n_{s_k}(c_k) contained in B°^n_{R_k}(0), with f_k Lipschitz on R^n and f_k = g_k on the closed ball (so f_k is C^1 on the open ball B_k, with Df_k = Dg_k continuous there; nothing is claimed outside B_k), such that, with F_k(w) := q_k(graphPoint(w, f_k(w))) and G_k := F_k(B_k), M is contained in N_0 cup U_k G_k.

5. Conclusions (0) and (1). Apply step 2 to each (q_k, f_k, R_k) and obtain H^n-null sets Z^k. E := N_0 cup U_k Z^k is H^n-null, so mu(E) = 0. Each x in M \ E lies in some G_k, contained in F_k(B°^n_{R_k}(0)), so HasWeighted(x, P^k_{a_k(x)}): this is (0). For such x, theta(x) > 0, so by 1(c) p_x = (P^k_{a_k(x)}).starProjection with finrank n: this is (1). Since mu(R^{n+l} \ M) = 0, both hold mu-a.e.

6. Conclusion (2). For each k, Pi_k(x) := orthogonal projection onto DF_k(a_k(x))(R^n) is continuous on G_k: a_k is continuous, w |-> Df_k(w) = Dg_k(w) is continuous on the open ball B_k, and the orthogonal projection onto the range of the injective linear map A_w := DF_k(w) is A_w (A_w^* A_w)^{-1} A_w^*, continuous in w. G_k is Borel (the continuous injective image of a sigma-compact set is sigma-compact). Define Pi(x) := Pi_k(x) for x in G_k \ U_{i<k} G_i and Pi(x) := 0 off U_k G_k. Pi is Borel measurable into the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps, and for x in M \ E, if x in G_k \ U_{i<k} G_i then x is not in Z^k, so p_x = Pi_k(x) = Pi(x) by step 5. Hence p = Pi mu-a.e., and x |-> p_x is AEStronglyMeasurable for mu.

7. Conclusion (3). Let x in M with HasWeighted(x, P) (mu-a.e. x by (0)). For e in (0,1) choose g_1, g_2 in C_c(R^{n+l}; [0,1]) with g_1 = 1 on B_{1-e}(0), spt g_1 in B_1(0), g_2 = 1 on B_1(0), spt g_2 in B_{1+e}(0). By 1(d), for r > 0 with B_{2r}(x) contained in U:
int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g_1(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) <= r^{-n} int_{M cap B_r(x)} theta dH^n = r^{-n} mu(B_r(x)) <= int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g_2(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y).
Letting r -> 0+ and then e -> 0, and using omega_n (1 - e)^n <= int_P g_1 dH^n <= int_P g_2 dH^n <= omega_n (1 + e)^n, we get mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x). As omega_n r^n is in (0, infinity), this is V.HasDensity x (theta x) (quotient in [0, infinity], limit ofReal theta(x)). Hence (3) holds mu-a.e.
proof_key_steps: mu is absolutely continuous w.r.t. H^n on M; uniqueness of weighted tangents identifies tangentProj with any weighted tangent plane on M
Graph lemma: area formula, Rademacher and Lebesgue points give the unweighted tangent plane of a Lipschitz graph
Upper density theorem for M \ Gamma and Gamma \ M, and Lebesgue points of theta
Weighted tangent plane of M equals the graph tangent plane H^n-a.e. on M cap Gamma: conclusion (4)
Cover M up to an H^n-null set by countably many C^1 graphs (Ch. 3 Lemma 1.2, implicit function theorem, McShane)
Existence and rank-n projection a.e.; a Borel representative gives measurability
Density equals multiplicity from the weighted blow-up limit

subproblems.title: Lebesgue measure of a parameter set is at most H^n of its rotated graph
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n, l, every linear isometry q of R^(n+l), every map u : R^n -> R^l and every set A contained in R^n (no measurability or regularity assumed): L^n(A) <= H^n(q(graph u over A)), where graph u over A = {graphPoint(x, u(x)) : x in A}, graphPoint(x, y) = (x, y) in R^n x R^l = R^(n+l), L^n = volume on R^n and H^n = muHE[n] on R^(n+l).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (A : Set (Rn n)), volume A ≤ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (q '' graphOver u A)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the 1-Lipschitz left inverse pi of the graph map) together with step 5 (L^n(A') = H^n(pi(F(A'))) <= H^n(F(A')), using that pi is 1-Lipschitz and H^n = L^n on R^n). Notation: S := q(graph u over A) = {q(graphPoint(x, u x)) : x in A}.
1. Projection. Let pi : R^(n+l) -> R^n, pi(z) := (z_1, ..., z_n), the first n coordinates. In Lean this is WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => z (Fin.castAdd l i)).
   (a) pi(graphPoint(x, y)) = x, since graphPoint(x, y) = toLp (Fin.append x y) and Fin.append x y (Fin.castAdd l i) = x i (Fin.append_left).
   (b) For all z, z': |pi z - pi z'|^2 = sum over i < n of (z_i - z'_i)^2 <= sum over j < n + l of (z_j - z'_j)^2 = |z - z'|^2. To see this, split the sum over Fin (n + l) with Fin.sum_univ_add; the remaining part is a sum of squares, hence >= 0. So pi is 1-Lipschitz.
2. Left inverse. phi := pi o q^-1 is 1-Lipschitz, because q^-1 is an isometry. Also phi(q(graphPoint(x, u x))) = pi(graphPoint(x, u x)) = x, hence phi(S) = A.
3. Lipschitz image bound. On every metric space, muHE[n] = c_n muH[n] with the same scalar c_n = addHaarScalarFactor(volume on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), muH[n]), which depends only on n (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). By LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with K = 1 and d = n >= 0: muH[n](phi(S)) <= 1^n muH[n](S) = muH[n](S). Multiplying by c_n gives muHE[n](phi(S)) <= muHE[n](S).
4. Normalisation on R^n. muHE[n] = volume on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Therefore L^n(A) = muHE[n](A) = muHE[n](phi(S)) <= muHE[n](S) = H^n(q(graph u over A)). QED
proof_key_steps: The first-n-coordinates map pi is 1-Lipschitz and pi(graphPoint(x, y)) = x
phi = pi o q^-1 is 1-Lipschitz and maps q(graph u over A) onto A
Lipschitz image bound for muH[n], transported to muHE[n] = c_n muH[n] with the same c_n on both spaces
muHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure on R^n

subproblems.title: H^n on a set of positive lower density is dominated by the weight when theta >= 1
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a set in R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta), O an open set with mu(O) < infinity, and Gamma a subset of O. Assume theta >= 1 mu-a.e., and every y in Gamma has positive lower density: there are c > 0 and s_0 > 0 with ofReal(c s^n) <= mu(B_s(y)) for all 0 < s < s_0. Then H^n restricted to Gamma is <= mu as measures; in particular H^n(Gamma \ M) = 0, and H^n(B cap Gamma) <= mu(B) for every set B.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (O Γ : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen O → V.weight O < ⊤ → Γ ⊆ O → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, 1 ≤ V.mult x) → (∀ y ∈ Γ, ∃ c s₀ : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < s₀ ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < s₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (c * s ^ n) ≤ V.weight (closedBall y s)) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict Γ ≤ V.weight
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 and 4 of the parent proof (Gamma \ M is H^n-null by the Upper Density Theorem; H^n <= mu on Gamma because theta >= 1). Uses the sibling upper_density (Submission.aetp_upper_density_zero_ae). Notation: H := muHE[n] on R^(n+l), M := V.carrier (H-null-measurable), theta := V.mult (> 0 on M, and a.e.-measurable for H restricted to M), mu := V.weight = (H restricted to M).withDensity(ofReal o theta). B_r(x) is the closed ball and B°_r(x) the open ball.
1. A measurable core of M. M is H-null-measurable, so there is a Borel M_1 contained in M with M_1 = M H-a.e. (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then (H restricted to M)(complement of M_1) = (H restricted to M_1)(complement of M_1) = 0, because restrictions to a.e.-equal sets agree (Measure.restrict_congr_set, Measure.restrict_apply). mu is absolutely continuous with respect to H restricted to M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so mu(complement of M_1) = 0.
2. Upper density. A := O cap M_1 is Borel with mu(A) <= mu(O) < infinity. By upper_density applied to nu := mu and A: for H-a.e. x, if x is not in A, then mu(A cap B_r(x))/ofReal(r^n) -> 0 as r -> 0+.
3. H(Gamma \ M) = 0. Let x be in Gamma \ M; then x is not in A, since A is contained in M_1, which is contained in M. Let c, s_0 be as in the hypothesis for y = x, and e > 0 with B°_e(x) contained in O (O is open and contains x).
   For 0 < r < min(s_0, e/2), B_r(x) is contained in O. So B_r(x) \ A is contained in the complement of M_1, and mu(B_r(x) \ A) = 0 by step 1. Therefore
   ofReal(c r^n) <= mu(B_r(x)) <= mu(A cap B_r(x)) + mu(B_r(x) \ A) = mu(A cap B_r(x)),
   i.e. mu(A cap B_r(x))/ofReal(r^n) >= ofReal(c) > 0 (ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le, ofReal(c) ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(c r^n)).
   This holds for all r in the interval (0, min(s_0, e/2)), which belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0. If the quotient tended to 0, it would eventually be < ofReal(c) (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_lt_const). Since 𝓝[>] 0 is a proper filter, both eventual properties would hold at some r, a contradiction.
   Hence x lies in the exceptional H-null set of step 2. So Gamma \ M is contained in that set, and H(Gamma \ M) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
4. theta >= 1 H-a.e. on M. The hypothesis says 1 <= theta mu-a.e. The density ofReal o theta is a.e.-measurable for H restricted to M (V.aemeasurable_mult.ennreal_ofReal), so by ae_withDensity_iff', for (H restricted to M)-a.e. x: ofReal(theta x) != 0 implies 1 <= theta x. Also, for (H restricted to M)-a.e. x, x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀, M null-measurable), where theta x > 0 (V.mult_pos), so ofReal(theta x) != 0. Hence 1 <= ofReal(theta x) for (H restricted to M)-a.e. x.
5. Conclusion. As measures:
   H restricted to Gamma <= H restricted to M = (H restricted to M).withDensity 1 <= (H restricted to M).withDensity(ofReal o theta) = mu.
   The first inequality is Measure.restrict_mono_ae: Gamma is contained in M up to the H-null set Gamma \ M (step 3, ae_le_set). Then withDensity_one, and withDensity_mono with step 4. Equivalently, for every Borel B:
   H(B cap Gamma) <= H(B cap M) + H(Gamma \ M) = H(B cap M) <= integral over B of ofReal(theta) d(H restricted to M) = mu(B) (withDensity_apply).
   For an arbitrary set B: H(B cap Gamma) <= (H restricted to Gamma)(B) <= mu(B) (Measure.le_restrict_apply, Measure.le_iff'). In particular H(Gamma \ M) <= mu(complement of M) = 0. QED
proof_key_steps: Borel core M_1 of the carrier with mu(complement of M_1) = 0
Apply upper_density to mu and A = O cap M_1
Positive lower density at points of Gamma \ M contradicts zero density, so H^n(Gamma \ M) = 0
theta >= 1 H^n-a.e. on M via ae_withDensity_iff' and mult_pos
H^n restricted to Gamma <= H^n restricted to M = withDensity 1 <= withDensity(ofReal theta) = mu

subproblems.title: Area comparison and null-set transfer along a continuous graph piece dominated by a measure
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometry of R^(n+l), Omega a Borel subset of R^n, u : R^n -> R^l continuous on Omega, F(x) := q(graphPoint(x, u(x))), Gamma := q(graph u over Omega) = F(Omega), and nu a measure on R^(n+l) with H^n restricted to Gamma <= nu (H^n = muHE[n]). Then (a) for every Borel A contained in Omega, q(graph u over A) = F(A) is Borel; (b) for every Borel A contained in Omega and every Borel g : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity], the integral over A of g(F(x)) dL^n(x) is at most the integral over q(graph u over A) of g dnu; (c) for every property P of points of R^(n+l) that holds nu-a.e., P(F(x)) holds for L^n-a.e. x in Omega.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (Ω : Set (Rn n)), MeasurableSet Ω → ContinuousOn u Ω → ∀ ν : Measure (Amb n ℓ), (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict (q '' graphOver u Ω) ≤ ν → (∀ A : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ Ω → MeasurableSet (q '' graphOver u A)) ∧ (∀ A : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ Ω → ∀ g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → ∫⁻ x in A, g (q (graphPoint x (u x))) ≤ ∫⁻ y in q '' graphOver u A, g y ∂ν) ∧ ∀ P : Amb n ℓ → Prop, (∀ᵐ y ∂ν, P y) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict Ω), P (q (graphPoint x (u x)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 5 of the parent proof (Borel images by Lusin–Souslin; L^n(A') <= H^n(F(A')) <= mu(F(A')) gives (E1) through the push-forward F_#(L^n restricted to A), and transfers null sets to parameters). Here mu is replaced by any measure nu dominating H^n on the graph piece. Uses the sibling graph_volume (Submission.anyrad_gc_volume_le_graph_hausdorff). Notation: H := muHE[n] on R^(n+l). For every A, q(graph u over A) = F(A) (Set.image_image).
1. F is continuous on Omega and injective. graphPoint is continuous in (x, y): it is toLp o Fin.append applied to (ofLp x, ofLp y) (PiLp.continuous_toLp, PiLp.continuous_ofLp, Fin.continuous_append). The map x -> (x, u x) is continuous on Omega, and q is continuous, so F is continuous on Omega. If F x = F x', then graphPoint(x, u x) = graphPoint(x', u x') (q is injective); comparing the coordinates Fin.castAdd l i gives x = x'.
2. (a) Let A be Borel with A contained in Omega. F is continuous and injective on A, and R^n is a Polish space, so F(A) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
3. Key inequality. For every set S in R^(n+l):
   H(S cap Gamma) <= (H restricted to Gamma)(S) <= nu(S)
   by Measure.le_restrict_apply and the hypothesis applied to arbitrary sets (Measure.le_iff'). Combined with graph_volume (L^n(B) <= H(F(B)) for every B in R^n): if B is contained in Omega and F(B) is contained in S, then
   L^n(B) <= H(F(B)) <= H(S cap Gamma) <= nu(S).
4. (b) Let A be Borel with A contained in Omega, and g Borel. F is a.e.-measurable for L^n restricted to A (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable). Let m := F_#(L^n restricted to A) (Measure.map).
   For Borel B, m(B) = L^n(F^-1(B) cap A) (Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable, Measure.restrict_apply'). F(F^-1(B) cap A) is contained in (B cap F(A)) cap Gamma, so by step 3, m(B) <= nu(B cap F(A)) = (nu restricted to F(A))(B) (Measure.restrict_apply). Hence m <= nu restricted to F(A) (Measure.le_iff).
   Therefore: integral over A of g(F x) dx = integral of g dm (lintegral_map') <= integral of g d(nu restricted to F(A)) (lintegral_mono') = integral over q(graph u over A) of g dnu.
5. (c) Let P hold nu-a.e., i.e. nu({y : not P y}) = 0. Since Omega is Borel, (L^n restricted to Omega)({x : not P(F x)}) = L^n({x : not P(F x)} cap Omega) (Measure.restrict_apply'). The F-image of this set is contained in {y : not P y} cap Gamma, so by step 3 its L^n-measure is <= nu({y : not P y}) = 0. Hence P(F x) holds for L^n-a.e. x in Omega (ae_iff). QED
proof_key_steps: F = q o graphPoint(., u(.)) is continuous on Omega and injective
Lusin–Souslin gives Borel images F(A)
graph_volume plus H^n restricted to Gamma <= nu give L^n(B) <= nu(S) whenever F(B) is contained in S
The push-forward of L^n restricted to A is <= nu restricted to F(A); lintegral_map' gives (b)
nu-null sets pull back to L^n-null parameter sets in Omega: (c)

subproblems.title: Tangent planes along a C^1 graph piece, given the transfer of weight-null sets to parameters
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U open in R^(n+l), V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu = V.weight, q a linear isometry of R^(n+l), Omega open in R^n, u : R^n -> R^l of class C^1 on Omega, and F(x) := q(graphPoint(x, u(x))). Assume that for every property P which holds mu-a.e., P(F(x)) holds for L^n-a.e. x in Omega. Then for L^n-a.e. x in Omega, V.tangentProj(F(x)) is the orthogonal projection onto the image under q of span{graphPoint(v, Du(x) v) : v in R^n} (Du(x) = fderiv u x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (Ω : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen Ω → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u Ω → (∀ P : Amb n ℓ → Prop, (∀ᵐ y ∂V.weight, P y) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict Ω), P (q (graphPoint x (u x)))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict Ω), V.tangentProj (q (graphPoint x (u x))) = (Submodule.map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (fderiv ℝ u x v)))).starProjection
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof ("locality of approximate tangents, Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), identifies p on the graph with q(graph Du) a.e.") and step 5 (null sets transfer to parameters). The locality statement is taken from the sibling tangent_facts (Submission.ted_tangent_plane_facts, conjunct (4)). That conjunct proves, for Lipschitz graphs, exactly the blow-up identification of step 6: Lebesgue points of theta on the graph, zero density of M \ Gamma and Gamma \ M, and convergence of the blown-up graphs to the tangent plane. Its exceptional set is mu-null, which the transfer hypothesis handles. Notation: T(x) := image under q of span{graphPoint(v, Du(x) v) : v in R^n}, i.e. Submodule.map q (span (range (v -> graphPoint v (Du(x) v)))).
1. Regularity of u. u is C^1 on the open set Omega. So u is differentiable at every x in Omega (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn_one, and Omega is a neighbourhood of x), and x -> Du(x) is continuous on Omega (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).
2. Local Lipschitz extension. Fix x_0 in Omega and e > 0 with B°_e(x_0) contained in Omega. Put r := e/2 and K := B_r(x_0) (closed ball); K is contained in Omega and is compact and convex.
   ||Du|| is continuous on K, hence bounded there by some C (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). By the mean value inequality on the convex set K, u is L-Lipschitz on K with L := max(C, 0) (Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le).
   Extend u restricted to K to a map f : R^n -> R^l that is Lipschitz on all of R^n and equals u on K. One way is LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension. Another is a coordinatewise McShane extension (LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi for x -> ofLp(u x), then toLp, which is Lipschitz as a linear map between finite-dimensional spaces).
   Put R := |x_0| + r. Then B°_r(x_0) is contained in B°_R(0) (triangle inequality), and f is Lipschitz on B_R(0).
3. Apply tangent_facts (4) to q, f, R and the Lipschitz constant of f. It gives a mu-a.e. property Q(y):
   "for all x' in B°_R(0), if y = q(graphPoint(x', f x')) and f is differentiable at x', then V.tangentProj y is the orthogonal projection onto span{q(graphPoint(v, Df(x') v)) : v in R^n}".
   By the transfer hypothesis, Q(F x) holds for L^n-a.e. x in Omega.
4. Let x in B°_r(x_0) satisfy Q(F x).
   (a) x lies in B°_R(0), and f(x) = u(x) since x is in K; so F x = q(graphPoint(x, f x)).
   (b) f = u on the open ball B°_r(x_0), a neighbourhood of x. Hence f is differentiable at x, because u is (step 1; DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq), and Df(x) = Du(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
   (c) So Q(F x) gives V.tangentProj(F x) = orthogonal projection onto span{q(graphPoint(v, Du(x) v))}.
   (d) span{q(w) : w in W} = map q (span W) with W := range(v -> graphPoint(v, Du(x) v)) (Submodule.map_span, Set.range_comp). This is T(x), so V.tangentProj(F x) = T(x).starProjection. In Lean, prove the submodule equality first and conclude by congr, since starProjection carries an instance argument.
   Hence the set of x in Omega cap B°_r(x_0) where the conclusion fails is L^n-null.
5. Local to global. Every x_0 in Omega has a neighbourhood B°_r(x_0) on which the failure set is L^n-null (step 4). R^n is second countable, so countably many of these balls cover Omega, and the failure set in Omega is L^n-null. One can use measure_null_of_locally_null, or a countable cover by balls with centres in a countable dense set and rational radii together with ae_all_iff. Together with ae_restrict_mem (Omega is open, hence Borel), this is the claim: for L^n-a.e. x in Omega, V.tangentProj(F x) = T(x).starProjection. QED
proof_key_steps: u is differentiable on Omega with continuous Du
On a closed ball K in Omega u is Lipschitz (mean value inequality); extend to a globally Lipschitz f equal to u on K
tangent_facts (4) for (q, f, R) gives the graph tangent identity mu-a.e.; transfer it to parameters
On the open ball f = u near x, so Df(x) = Du(x) and span{q(graphPoint(v, Du v))} = q(span{graphPoint(v, Du v)})
Countably many balls (Lindelöf / measure_null_of_locally_null) give the L^n-a.e. statement on Omega

subproblems.title: Quadratic Lebesgue points of a bounded operator field for a measure finite on an open set
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, mu a measure on R^(n+l), O an open set with mu(O) < infinity, and g : R^(n+l) -> L(R^(n+l), R^(n+l)) mu-a.e. strongly measurable with operator norm ||g(w)|| <= C for every w. Then for mu-a.e. y in O, mu(B_s(y))^-1 times the integral over B_s(y) of hsNormSq(g(w) - g(y)) dmu(w) tends to 0 in [0, infinity] as s -> 0+ (B_s(y) closed balls; hsNormSq the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (O : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen O → μ O < ⊤ → ∀ (g : Amb n ℓ → (Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ)) (C : ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable g μ → (∀ w, ‖g w‖ ≤ C) → ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, y ∈ O → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (μ (closedBall y s))⁻¹ * ∫⁻ w in closedBall y s, ENNReal.ofReal (hsNormSq (g w - g y)) ∂μ) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation for the finite measure mu restricted to an open ball, Simon Ch. 1, 3.23; Mathlib Besicovitch.vitaliFamily with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt). The parent's bound |p_y| <= sqrt n is replaced by an operator-norm bound C. Notation: N := n + l, B_s(y) closed balls, e_i the standard basis vectors.
1. Hilbert–Schmidt versus operator norm. For a linear map A of R^N, hsNormSq(A) = sum over i < N of |A e_i|^2 <= N ||A||^2, because |A e_i| <= ||A|| |e_i| = ||A|| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). Also C >= 0 (as 0 <= ||g(0)|| <= C) and ||g(w) - g(y)|| <= ||g(w)|| + ||g(y)|| <= 2C. Hence hsNormSq(g w - g y) <= N (2C) ||g w - g y||. With K := ofReal(2 N C) < infinity:
   ofReal(hsNormSq(g w - g y)) <= K ||g w - g y||ₑ for all w, y.
2. The finite measure. mu_O := mu restricted to O has mu_O(R^N) = mu(O) < infinity, so it is a finite measure (hence locally finite and s-finite). g is a.e. strongly measurable for mu_O and bounded by C, so g is mu_O-integrable (Integrable.of_bound).
3. Differentiation. R^N is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so it has the Besicovitch covering property and is second countable. Apply Lebesgue's differentiation theorem along the Besicovitch Vitali family of mu_O (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div_of_integrable for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily mu_O): for mu_O-a.e. y,
   (integral over a of ||g w - g y||ₑ dmu_O(w)) / mu_O(a) -> 0 as a shrinks to y along the family.
   Compose with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt (closed balls B_s(y), s -> 0+): for mu_O-a.e. y,
   Q_y(s) := (integral over B_s(y) of ||g w - g y||ₑ dmu_O) / mu_O(B_s(y)) -> 0 as s -> 0+.
   Since O is Borel, "mu_O-a.e. y" means "mu-a.e. y, provided y is in O" (ae_restrict_iff').
4. Comparison and squeeze. Fix such a y in O and e > 0 with B°_e(y) contained in O. For 0 < s < e, B_s(y) is contained in O, so mu_O(B_s(y)) = mu(B_s(y)) and mu_O restricted to B_s(y) equals mu restricted to B_s(y) (Measure.restrict_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset). By step 1 and lintegral_const_mul':
   mu(B_s(y))^-1 · integral over B_s(y) of ofReal(hsNormSq(g w - g y)) dmu <= mu(B_s(y))^-1 · K · integral over B_s(y) of ||g w - g y||ₑ dmu = K Q_y(s).
   Here a / b = b^-1 a in [0, infinity]; if mu(B_s(y)) = 0, both sides are 0 since infinity · 0 = 0.
   As K < infinity, K Q_y(s) -> K · 0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). The left side is >= 0, and the bound holds for s in (0, e), an element of 𝓝[>] 0. So the left side tends to 0 by the squeeze theorem (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'). This holds for mu-a.e. y in O. QED
proof_key_steps: hsNormSq(A) <= (n+l)||A||^2 and ||g w - g y|| <= 2C give ofReal(hsNormSq(g w - g y)) <= K ||g w - g y||
mu restricted to O is finite, so the bounded field g is integrable for it
Besicovitch–Lebesgue differentiation along closed balls for mu restricted to O
Small balls around y in O see mu and mu restricted to O alike; squeeze with K times the L^1 averages
